about.title: About SnapPVD
about.tagline: An independent community project — not the City of Providence.
about.what.p1: SnapPVD is a free tool for reporting a problem in Providence — a pothole, a broken street light, a missed trash pickup, illegal dumping, an abandoned vehicle, a parking issue, and more — from your phone in about 30 seconds. You pick the problem, add a photo and a location, and we file it with the city's official 311 system for you.
about.who.p1: We're neighbors running this as a volunteer community project. We are not the City of Providence, and we are not affiliated with or endorsed by the city — we just wanted to make 311 reporting easier for the people around us. The city's official 311 lives at
about.flow.1.b: Pick the problem, snap a photo, confirm the address, and tap send.
about.flow.2.b: Every report gets a quick check — is it inside Providence, is it a duplicate, does it have what the city needs — with a person in the loop before it goes out.
about.flow.3.b: We submit it to the city's official 311 on your behalf, using a project-owned account.
about.flow.4.b: The city assigns a 311 case number and works your report like any other request. Follow it any time from the tracking link we give you — no account needed.
about.emergency.p1: If someone is in danger, call 911. SnapPVD is for non-urgent city problems, and reports are reviewed and filed by people, so they take time. For anything hazardous — a gas leak, a downed power line, a fire, flooding — call 911 or the utility directly.
about.record.p1: Once we file it, your report — the photo, location, and description — becomes a public record in the city's 311 system and shows up on the city's public feed. That's how 311 works, and we can't undo it.
about.record.for: for what we keep and how it's handled.
about.seasonal.p1: Some categories only appear when they're relevant. Winter problems like unshoveled sidewalks and unplowed streets show up roughly November through March and are hidden the rest of the year, so the list stays short and matches what the city is handling that season.
about.diy.pre: You can always report straight to the city at
about.diy.post: , or by phone. Using SnapPVD is completely optional — it just saves you a few steps.
about.contact.p1: Questions, feedback, or a problem with a report? Email us at
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.tagline: An independent community project — not the City of Providence.
privacy.intro: SnapPVD is a free, volunteer-run project. We keep this simple: we collect only what we need to file your report with the city, and nothing else. We never sell your information. Here's the whole picture.
privacy.record.p1: The big thing to know: once we file your report with the city, it becomes a public record in the City of Providence's 311 system. Reports appear on the city's public feed, where anyone can see them. We can't undo that.
privacy.collect.report.b: The problem category, the address and location (from your photo, your phone's GPS, or what you type), an optional description, an optional photo, and any per-category answers — for example, the size of a pothole. This is the report; we collect it to file it with the city.
privacy.collect.contact.t: Your name and email — only if you give them.
privacy.collect.contact.b: Both are optional; you can report anonymously. If you add your email, we pass it to the city so they can send you their own updates on the report. We don't use it for anything else — no newsletters, no marketing.
privacy.collect.device.b: Your browser sends a random ID — no login, no account, no name attached — so we can space out submissions (one report at a time) and slow down abuse. It isn't used to track you across the web.
privacy.collect.offline.t: An offline copy on your device.
privacy.collect.offline.b: If you send a report while offline, it's saved in your browser's storage on your own phone and goes out automatically once you're back online. That copy stays on your device until it's sent.
privacy.token.p1: When you send a report, we give you a private tracking link with a long, random token in it — no account to log into. Anyone with the link can see that report's status, so keep it to yourself, but the token can't be guessed. Your links are saved in this browser under My reports.
privacy.storage.p1: Your report and any photo are stored on our servers, hosted by an infrastructure provider in the United States that stores and moves the data on our behalf and does not use it for its own purposes. When you submit, we also run an automated bot check to keep out spam.
privacy.who.city.b: Once we file your report, it's a public record in the city's 311 system and on its public feed — the photo, location, description, and any name you added are public.
privacy.who.infra.b: As described above, only to store and move the data for us.
privacy.who.team.b: To review reports and file them with the city.
privacy.who.sold.b: We don't sell your information, and we don't share it beyond what's needed to file and track your report. No ads.
privacy.retention.photo.b: We automatically delete your photo about 30 days after the city marks the case resolved.
privacy.retention.record.b: We trim a report down to the minimum once it's resolved, keeping only what we need to show its history.
privacy.retention.city.b: Once a report is filed, the city keeps its own copy under its own rules. We don't control that copy.
privacy.choices.anon.b: Name and email are optional — leave them blank and we still file your report.
privacy.choices.delete.t: Ask us to delete our copy.
privacy.choices.delete.b: Email us and we'll delete the copy on our side. We can't delete what the city already holds — once a report is a public record with Providence, only the city can remove it.
privacy.children.p1: SnapPVD is meant for residents reporting city problems. It isn't directed at children under 13, and we don't knowingly collect information from them.
privacy.changes.p1: If we change how we handle your information, we'll update this page and the date below.
privacy.contact.p1: Questions about privacy, or a deletion request? Email us at
